nodes.body: The false-capability path currently only points back to `SupportsServiceConfiguration`; it does not give the actionable alternative required by #105/design section 9 (configure the distributed resource through its supported environment/configuration surface or mock an HTTP boundary). Since this exception is the first feedback a Tier 2 caller receives, include that guidance in the message rather than requiring the caller to infer it from the flag.

Good catch — updated the exception message to point at the actual Tier 2 alternatives (configuring the resource's environment/configuration surface, or mocking the HTTP boundary via something like WireMock.Net.Aspire) instead of just referencing the flag. Also fixed the "where"/"when" doc wording, clarified in the design doc that `TestSetUp.ConfigureServices` is a separate entry point outside this guard's scope, and bumped `Common.targets` to 5.12.0 to match the CHANGELOG entry. See 26a3d18.

The snapshot and watermark update are not atomic: if a resource log is enqueued after `buffer.Skip(lastCount).ToArray()` but before `buffer.Count` is read, the new count advances past an entry that was never returned or checked. That entry is then skipped forever, which can hide output and bypass the streaming error check under normal concurrent logging. Use an atomic drain/sequence boundary rather than a separate enumeration and count read.

Making `TesterBaseCore` the new declaration site for the existing public/protected tester surface is a binary breaking change, not just an inheritance refactor: previously compiled consumers reference members such as `TesterBase.get_Implementor`, `TesterBase.get_SetUp`, and `TesterBase.JsonMediaTypeNames`, but those metadata members no longer exist on `TesterBase`. Such consumers will fail with missing-method/member errors after upgrading to v5.12.0; retain forwarding members on `TesterBase` (or use a major-version breaking change) if binary compatibility is required.

This issue also appears on line 153 of the same file.
Understood. Conscience decision to move as a testing package.

Replacing the existing `Delay(TimeSpan)`/`Delay(int)` methods with nullable/optional-parameter signatures is a binary breaking change in v5.12.0: already-compiled consumers still reference the old method signatures and will fail with `MissingMethodException` after upgrading. Keep the original overloads as forwarding compatibility methods and add the reason-capable overloads instead.
Understood. Conscience decision to move as a testing package.

Changing this public virtual hook's parameter from `TesterBase` to `TesterBaseCore` silently stops existing `TesterExtensionsConfig` overrides from being invoked: compiled extensions retain the old override, while `HttpResponseMessageAssertorBase` now dispatches to the new no-op method. This can make custom response-value enrichment disappear without a compile error in consuming tests; preserve/bridge the old virtual hook while adding the Aspire-capable path.
Understood. Conscience decision to move as a testing package.

Changing these public/protected constructors from `TestServer` to `IHttpClientSource` is source-breaking for consumers who derive from `HttpTesterBase`/`HttpTester<T>` or construct `ControllerTester` directly. Existing Tier 1 extensions cannot compile against the new package even though the release is a minor version; please retain compatibility overloads that adapt a `TestServer`, or otherwise document/version this as a breaking change.
Understood. Conscience decision to move as a testing package.

This changes the public constructor signature from `(TesterBase, TestServer)` to `(TesterBaseCore, IHttpClientSource)`. Existing consumers that compiled against the former constructor (including custom `HttpTester` subclasses) will fail at runtime with `MissingMethodException` when this minor-version package is upgraded; retain a compatibility constructor or make the breaking API change explicit with an appropriate major-version strategy. The same issue applies to the other public tester/assertor constructors changed to `TesterBaseCore`.
Understood. Conscience decision to move as a testing package.
